questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Provoke
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Pacify.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Provoke"** means to stimulate or give rise to a reaction or emotion, typically a strong or unwelcome one, in someone. (उकसाना)

 
 
• **Example:** His speech was intended to **provoke **anger among the audience.
 
 
 
• **"Pacify"** means to bring peace to or calm down; to soothe. (शांत करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The mother tried to **pacify **her crying baby with a lullaby.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'Provoke'** is **'Pacify'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Incite** (उकसाना): Encourage or stir up (violent or unlawful behaviour).

 
 
• **Example:** The leader's speech was accused of **inciting **violence among the crowd.
 
 
 
• **Agitate** (उत्तेजित करना): Make someone troubled or nervous.
 
 
• **Example:** The news of the accident **agitated **him greatly.
 
 
 
• **Aggravate** (बिगाड़ना): Make (a problem, injury, or offense) worse or more serious.
 
 
• **Example:** Scratching the rash will only **aggravate **it.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

They will publish the research findings in a scientific journal next month.

options.text: The research findings will be published in a scientific journal by them.
The research findings will be published in a scientific journal by them next month.
The research findings will have been published in a scientific journal by them next month.
The research findings will be being published in a scientific journal by them next month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "They will publish the research findings in a scientific journal next month."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the research findings" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "will publish" to "will be published" (future simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "them."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "next month" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The research findings will be published in a scientific journal by them next month."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"They will publish the research findings in a scientific journal next month." – This is the active voice version of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3: **"The research findings will have been published by them in a scientific journal next month." – Incorrect tense (future perfect passive).
 
• **Option 4: **"The research findings will be being published in a scientific journal by them next month." – Incorrect use of future continuous passive.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The smoke coming out of the factory chimneys was polluting the air, which was becoming a major _______ for the local residents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**concern**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the impact of pollution on residents caused by factory smoke.
 
• The appropriate noun should indicate something that causes worry or distress to the residents.
 
• "**Concern**" fits well as it denotes a source of worry or distress, which aligns with the context of pollution affecting the local residents.
 
• Other options ("**law**", "**area**", "**idea**") do not fit the context of describing the impact of pollution on the residents.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *The smoke coming out of the factory chimneys was polluting the air, which was becoming a major **concern__** for the local residents.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Law **(कानून): "Law" means a system of rules, which does not fit the context of discussing the impact of pollution.
 
• **Area **(क्षेत्र): "Area" means a region or part of a town, which cannot describe the residents' worries stemming from pollution.
 
• **Idea **(विचार): "Idea" means a thought or suggestion, which does not reflect the distress caused by pollution.

questions.question:

The Namesake was written by Jhumpa Lahiri.

options.text: Jhumpa Lahiri has written The Namesake.
Jhumpa Lahiri was writing The Namesake.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The Namesake was written by Jhumpa Lahiri."
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the original subject "Jhumpa Lahiri" at the beginning.
 
• Change the passive verb form "was written" to "wrote" (past simple active).
 
• Ensure the object "The Namesake" follows the verb for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3: **"Jhumpa Lahiri was writing The Namesake." – Incorrect aspect (past continuous instead of past simple).

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **A white elephant**.

__
 
• The word **"A white elephant"** means something that has cost a lot of money but has no useful purpose. (बहुत महंगा लेकिन बेकार चीज़)

 
 
• **Example:** The new stadium is a white elephant that no one uses.
 
 
 
• **Explanation:** In the given sentence, "His old car has become a financial burden on him now," the idiom "A white elephant" appropriately describes the car as something costly to maintain but of little value. (उसकी पुरानी कार अब उसके लिए एक आर्थिक बोझ बन गई है)
 
 
• **Example:** The old mansion he inherited turned out to be a white elephant; it required constant repairs and maintenance.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** His daughter is the apple of his eye.
 
 
 
• **An eyesore** (आंखों में चुभने वाली चीज़): Something that is very ugly or unpleasant to look at.
 
 
• **Example:** The abandoned building is an eyesore in the neighborhood.
 
 
 
• **A rare bird** (एक दुर्लभ पक्षी): A person or thing that is unusual or exceptional.
 
 
• **Example:** She's a rare bird in the world of classical music.

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) her suburbs, she was enthralled to see

(B) one cold evening, when she went

(C) autumn still attached to

(D) the last golden leaf left from

(E) out for a walk on the snowy paths of

(F) an otherwise leafless tree
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The paragraph starts with an introduction to the setting, which is provided by **sentence B**: **"One cold evening, when she went"**
 
• Next, **sentence E** follows logically as it describes where she went: "out for a walk on the snowy paths of"
 
• Then, **sentence A** introduces the specific location and her reaction: "her suburbs, she was enthralled to see"
 
• **Sentence D** follows as it describes the sight that enthralled her: "the last golden leaf left from"
 
• **Sentence C** provides context to the leaf by explaining the season: "autumn still attached to"
 
• Finally, the paragraph concludes with **sentence F**: "an otherwise leafless tree."

Hence, the correct Order of the sentence is **B, E, A, D, C, F. (BEADCF)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (BADECF)** is incorrect because it does not establish where she was walking first, making the sequence less coherent.
 
• **Option 3 (CAFEDB)** is incorrect because it starts with autumn and the leaf, providing context out of order before introducing the setting and action.
 
• **Option 4 (CABEDF)** is incorrect because it starts with autumn, disrupting the logical flow of introducing the action and the setting first.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The Colonel said that it gave him great pleasure to be there that evening.

options.text: The Colonel said, “It gives me great pleasure to be here this evening.”
The Colonel said, “It gave me great pleasure to be there that evening.”
The Colonel says, “It gives me great pleasure to be there that evening.”
The Colonel said, “It gave him great pleasure to be there that evening.”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** The Colonel said that it gave him great pleasure to be there that evening.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **“It gave him great pleasure to be there that evening” becomes “It gives me great pleasure to be here this evening”**
 
 
• Indirect “It gave him” is converted to direct “It gives me” with pronoun change.
 
• “there” is changed to “here” to match direct speech context.
 
• “that evening” is changed to “this evening” for present tense context.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Remains “said” in both indirect and direct forms.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter “It” and ends with a period.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Example of a Different Direct Speech Conversion:** *The Colonel said, “It gives me great pleasure to be here this evening.”*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** “The Colonel said, ‘It gave me great pleasure to be there that evening.’” 

 
 
• Maintains past tense, does not match present context of the event.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** “The Colonel says, ‘It gives me great pleasure to be there that evening.’” 
 
 
• Incorrect reporting verb tense, changes meaning to a general statement.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** “The Colonel said, ‘It gave him great pleasure to be there that evening.’” 
 
 
• Incorrect pronoun “him” used, changes the meaning.

questions.question:
The following sentence may have an error of article. Choose the correct sentence from the given options. Choose ‘No error’ if the sentence has no error.

The festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people.

options.text: An festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people.
Festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people.
The festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate minds of people.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the unnecessary use of the article "**the**" before the term "**festivals**."
 
• When referring to festivals in general, no article is needed.
 
• The correct sentence should be "**Festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "An festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate the minds of people" **– This option incorrectly uses "An" before a plural noun.
 
• **Option 2: "No error" **– This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but the sentence has an error.
 
• **Option 4: "The festivals are celebrated everywhere to rejuvenate minds of people" **– This option incorrectly omits "the" before "minds of people."

• **"Obliterated" **refers to something that has been wiped out or utterly destroyed. (विलुप्त करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The ancient manuscript was **obliterated **by the fire.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of **'annihilated' **is **'obliterated'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Omitted **(छोड़ना): To leave out or exclude.

 
 
• **Example:** He **omitted **the second chapter from his report.
 
 
 
• **Occluded **(अवरोधित): To block or obstruct.
 
 
• **Example: **An **occluded **artery can lead to serious health problems.
 
 
 
• **Obstructed** (रोकना): To block or hinder progress.
 
 
• **Example:** The fallen tree **obstructed **the road.
